insight.title: Why Working Harder Won’t Solve Your Recurring Problems
insight.subtitle: How to spot when more effort is actually making your problem worse

sections.text: In 1894, newspapers predicted that every street in London would soon be buried under nine feet of horse manure. Experts were certain the city’s growth would lead to its inevitable, filthy collapse.

The error was linear thinking. They tried to optimize the horse-drawn world with better shovels, never imagining the motor engine would arrive to make the entire problem of manure irrelevant within a decade.
When we plan for the future, we often try to solve new challenges with more "shoveling." We assume the solution is more intensity, rather than realizing our current tool is simply the wrong fit.
Try this today: The next time you face a recurring obstacle today, consider changing the tool instead of the effort.
True breakthroughs don't solve your current problems; they make them irrelevant.
